subject: fiml: total sample vs. used sample

messages.author: 8c68636401b6ddd4
messages.subject: fiml: total sample vs. used sample
parts:
Hi all,

I have a sample of approximately 2000 cases, but only for one variable (lets call it var1). For other two study variables (var2 and var3) I have data only from a much smaller sample (i.e., n=400). When I include var1 and var2 in my model and use the fiml (i.e., estimator = "MLR", missing = "ML"), the entire sample will be used. However, when I include all variables in the model (e.g., a regression between var2 and var3), the output gives the following:

Number of observations: used 400, total 2000.

Does this mean that using fiml does not help if both study variables (i.e., a regression between var2 and var3) have many missings? Is imputation the only way that would me allow to use the entire sample in this case?

Thanks in advance!

Best,
Annaleena

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: fiml: total sample vs. used sample
parts:
when I include all variables in the model (e.g., a regression between var2 and var3), the output gives the following:

Number of observations: used 400, total 2000.

Does this mean that using fiml does not help

If one of the incomplete variables is exogenous, you would need to set missing = "fiml.x" to incorporate the same method for those predictors, or set fixed.x=FALSE so that the exogenous predictors are also treated as random variables.
